 Arthur Rinderknech turned his match around against Francisco Cerundolo before the Argentine retired injured, while Quentin Halys delivered a solid win over Arthur Fery. Both Frenchmen move on at the Rolex Paris Masters.
 Arthur Rinderknech during the second round of the US Open. © TIMOTHY A. CLARY AFP Clément Gehl 03/11/2026, 12:30 1 min to read Follow us ATP Masters 1000 Cerúndolo Fery Halys Paris Rinderknech To open Tuesday's action at the Rolex Paris Masters, two Frenchmen were in action: Arthur Rinderknech and Quentin Halys.
 The first faced Francisco Cerundolo, ranked No. 20 in the world. Things started badly for Rinderknech, who was broken right away.
 Remove ads Cerundolo served for the match before getting injured
 After dropping the first set 6-3, he saw his opponent break in the ninth game and earn the chance to serve for the match.
 But the Argentine then completely collapsed, losing the tie-break seven points to two. Broken right away in the third set by Rinderknech, Cerundolo, injured, decided to retire.
 The Frenchman will face Mattia Bellucci in the next round, who eliminated Lorenzo Sonego the day before.
 Solid serving performance from Halys
 As for Halys, he faced Arthur Fery, ranked No. 32 in the world. The first set was tight between the two players, who had to be separated by a tie-break.
 Although trailing five points to two, the Frenchman managed to turn things around and take it eight points to six.
 Despite facing three break points against him, he was the first to get the break in the 11th game and eventually won 7-6, 7-5.
 Halys will face Frances Tiafoe in the next round, who received a first-round bye.
